We want our children to be reflective, tolerant, active and successful British citizens within the global citizenship context.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Sandringham Primary School.
Sandringham is a successful primary school in the London Borough of Newham, with over 1000 children. Rated Outstanding by Ofsted in May 2017 and September 2023, the school serves a vibrant and diverse community and has children, speaking many different languages and celebrating most major world religions. This makes the school culturally rich, exciting and an interesting place to learn.
We are fully committed to working with parents to give children the very best start in their education. The school fundamentally understands the importance that all children must leave Sandringham at the end of year 6 literate and numerate. We know that for our children to be successful at the next stage of their learning, they must also be resilient and articulate learners. We have high expectations of everybody in our learning community. We work effectively together in making sure children understand they can always improve through hard work and dedication.
I am incredibly proud and privileged to be the Head Teacher of Sandringham Primary School.
Our children truly love coming to school. We want to provide a curriculum that is broad and balanced and values the arts, humanities, individual and team sports. We teach the children through a skills based curriculum which makes our children inquisitive, curious and learners for life.
We encourage you to visit Sandringham and see for yourself our happy, smiling children engaged in their learning.
I look forward to getting to know you and your family, whether your child is joining our Daycare, Sandringham Central or starting their statutory schooling.
Robert Cleary Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Bow Arts Project Day 4 | Sandringham Primary School
pageCache.text:
Bow Arts Project Day 4
The last of Year 3 completed the sculpting of their Elephant Hawk Moths today. Helped by some Year 6 Art Leaders, the children have now completed over 100 moths which await temperatures of over 1000 degrees in the school kiln before they are glazed. Some of the moths will find their way onto the sculptures due to be built in the school sensory garden.
Share this post

3B Mondrian Art
3B painted trees as starting points and then changed the shape and overall appearance by combining their ideas and images of Piet Mondrian’s work. They used mostly Primary Colours, to the black patterned lines they added as starting points for their new paintings.
Share this post

pageCache.pageTitle: Art Matters Photoshoot 2023 | Sandringham Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art Matters Photoshoot 2023
Year 5 and 6 children took part in the Art Matters Publicity Photoshoot at the Docklands Campus of the University of East London. They had been working for several weeks on a jewelry project where they used recycled materials, clay, nuts and bolts, and anything else they deemed useful to make their own ornamental pieces. The artwork represented different aspects in each child's life and told their story as a piece of jewelry. The children were professionally photographed in a studio with the final images forming the Art Matters posters that will advertise this year's exhibition held in July.
Share this post

pageCache.pageTitle: Sandringham Central - Maintained Nursery | Sandringham Primary School
pageCache.text:
Sandringham Central - Maintained Nursery
Sandringham Central caters for families with two and three year old children. We have places in our Nursery for two year old children with eligibility for a funded place. Parents can check their eligibility for a government funded 2 year old space by checking the criteria set out on the local council website: Newham Families: Free Early Education for Two Year Olds
We also offer spaces for two year old children from working families and the eligibility criteria and application process can be found here: Gov.UK Sign in to your childcare account. The places are 15 hour funded for our 2 year olds which consist of Monday - Friday either 8:45-11:45am or 12:30 - 3:30pm.
Sandringham Central also caters for three and four year old children. We have provision for 15 hour national offer places in our morning session running from 8:45-11:45 and in our afternoon session running from 12:30 – 3:30. All children are eligible for a 15 hour place and there are no eligibility checks to be completed.
As part of our total numbers, a total of 16 three year old children access a limited 16 space provision for families eligible for 30 hours running from 8:45 – 3:30 daily with the exception of Friday afternoons which are charged at an additional rate of £30. Parents can check their eligibility for government funded 30-hour spaces by creating a Childcare Choices account through the Gov.uk website.
The Sandringham Central building is purpose built learning space with its own entrance from Henderson Road. Throughout Sandringham Central, the children have access to a continuous provision of open-ended resources both indoors and outdoors, all year round. We believe there is no such thing as bad weather, as long as children are dressed appropriately to be outdoors. Sun, rain, wind and snow all add a valuable natural dynamic to learning opportunities. Throughout a child’s time in Sandringham Central, adults get to know the children well and consistently refer to the Development Matters Standards framework to track children’s progress and plan for next steps in learning. There is a heavy focus on developing children’s social, emotional, communication and physical skills before focussing on gaining knowledge in areas like: maths, writing and reading.
To find out more about the curriculum and ways parents can support their child at home please follow the link to The Department for Education document “What to Expect, When”
“Children learn gradually and continuously in social contexts through interactions and communications with others”
An age appropriate, topic based curriculum is planned with strong links to core texts in order to expose children to new ideas, concepts and ways of thinking. The staff throughout Foundation Stage are trained to support the children to engage in play opportunities, which have been planned to match individual interests. Children are encouraged to be independent and take on challenges to extend their thinking and develop skills. They are encouraged to be cooperative with their peers and confident to take appropriate risks.
We are driven by sets of principles which underpin our practice and provision. These principles draw upon key educational research and best practice for children aged at specific age phases. They inform on how we settle the children during their induction as well as the play based approach to learning. This ensures we have a values lead provision which puts the children at the centre of everything we do.
If you are interested in registering for your child's place at Sandringham Central, please complete the form on the link at the bottom of the page or alternatively you can print the registration form and return back to the school office once completed.

Breakfast Club
Sandringham Primary School before school child care - Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club offers child care before the start of the school day.
Parents and carers can drop children off from 7:30am. A healthy breakfast is served until 8:10am, after which children can enjoy supervised play activities before the school day begins and then dropped off in their class lines at the start of the school day.
There are limited spaces for pre-school aged children, but as a school we will always seek to accommodate families where there is a need. Please book in advance to allow us to manage food and staffing levels. The cost of breakfast club is £3 per child this should be paid in advance.
Please complete a form for each individual child in your family who needs before school care.
Follow this link to book: https://forms.gle/t7KsAqiueUiyAeF89
Breakfast Club Positive Behaviour Expectations
Be Kind and Respectful Speak politely to staff and other children. Use kind words and actions at all times.
Be Safe Walk indoors—no running or rough play. Follow adult instructions straight away.
Be Responsible Look after equipment, food, and the Breakfast Club space. Tidy up after yourself and help keep the area clean.
Include Everyone Be friendly and make sure no one is left out. Play and sit with different children if you can.
Be a Role Model Remember, Breakfast Club is for children of all ages.Older children should set a good example by showing the expected behaviour to younger ones—help them feel welcome and supported.
If Behaviour Becomes a Concern
If a child struggles to follow the behaviour expectations, staff will:
Give a gentle reminder or warning about the behaviour.
Share any ongoing concerns with parents or carers to work together in supporting positive choices.
If inappropriate behaviour continues, this may result in a child no longer being able to attend Breakfast Club.

pageCache.text:
SEND Specialist Autism Provision
SAP Autumn Term 1 - Wonderful Me and The Tiger who Came to Me
Wonderful Me
The purpose of this unit is to help with children’s transition to a new setting and settling back into the SAP. This unit provides children the opportunity to learn about everybody which helps with understanding the World and communication and language.
The Tiger who Came to Me
Children will be exploring a text, taking turns and sharing. They will have a tea party with friends.
SAP Summer Term - Let's Grow and Things that go
Let’s Grow
In this unit, children will be planting and watching things grow and creating a SAP garden.
Things that Go
In this unit, children will be learning about different types of transport. They will be making different types of transport to use within the setting from a range of materials. They will have the opportunity to have a trip on a bus.
SAP Spring Term - Seasons Come, Seasons Go and Can you find a Dinosaur?
Seasons Come, Seasons Go
In this unit, children will be learning about different seasons and exploring the outdoors. Children will have the opportunity to explore different sensory experiences (play snow, leaf printing etc).
Can you find a Dinosaur?
Children will have the opportunity to explore small world play with dinosaurs, moving in different ways and will have the opportunity for dancing sessions in afternoon sensory circuit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bow Arts Project Day 3 | Sandringham Primary School
pageCache.text:
Bow Arts Project Day 3
3A and 3B shared the day in the Art Room making Elephant Hawk-Moths with Bow Artist Miyuki Kasahara. They made them out of clay which will be fired in the kiln at about 1200 degrees centigrade. This means the final results will be stoneware, so hopefully the moths will not be porous and will be able to withstand the weather when they are on the new sculpture. The moth's name comes from the caterpillar's resemblance to an elephant's trunk. It is most common across Britain and Central Europe.
